The parties behind the programmes

A tokenized share depends on a series of named companies, and if any one of them fails, the holder can lose. This graph draws those parties: each issuer programme sits in the centre, the entities that issue, wrap, tokenize, keep the register, custody the underlying and verify the reserves sit around it, and the venues, regulators and permitted audiences sit on the rim. Every party edge comes from a cited dossier field and never from a press release. Every traded on edge is a sum of the programme's own pools and tickers, and its width is the log of that sum. Look for shared nodes: when one custodian or one exchange appears in four programmes, that is a concentration a table would hide.

What each colour is

How to read it

  • Node size is degree: a node is bigger because more programmes name it. It does not reflect the size of the business.
  • Edge width is the log of the edge weight, and the two weight families are scaled separately. A traded on edge weighs the summed pool liquidity of that programme's mints on that venue, falling back to summed 24-hour volume where the venue reports no pool. A CEX ticker never reports liquidity, so its width is a volume width and the side panel says so. Every other edge weighs the number of programmes that relation was read from, which is normally one, so those lines all draw at the base width. How many programmes name a party is shown by its node size.
  • Issues and references mean different things. A register-mirrored programme (one whose legal form is a registered share) tokenizes the listed company's own share, so the company issues it and the arrow runs company → programme. Every other programme only uses that company's price: the arrow is reversed, drawn as a dashed references line, and the company takes no part in the product. SpaceX is named by a Backpack dossier and its own prospectus never mentions the token.
  • A lends on edge carries no weight. The dossiers name the lending market in a sentence and give no number we can measure, so the line is a hairline and the quote is in the panel.
  • Focusing a programme dims everything more than two hops away. Nothing is removed, so the layout stays the same while you read one programme's parties.
  • An arrow reads as a sentence. Backed Assets (JE) Limited → wraps → xStocks; xStocks → regulated by → FMA Liechtenstein. The side panel spells out both directions.
  • A missing edge means the dossier does not name the party. A programme with no custodian edge has no custodian named in its documents. That is a gap in the disclosure; a custodian may still exist.
